name: GirlsWhoML & PhysicsX Hackathon
description:
## If commercial space flights land on Mars tomorrow, what would you build to create the Martian city?

[APPLICATIONS CLOSED]

[Join GirlsWhoML](https://www.girlswhoml.com/) [and PhysicsX](https://www.physicsx.ai/) for an evening hackathon in London to tackle the first human landing on Mars, supported by Cursor. You arrive on an empty, rust-red planet with no city, no roads, and no infrastructure. What do you build first?

You’ll design and prototype one core system for the Martian city, across three tracks: Architecture, Vehicles, and Life Support. Every build should combine engineering, machine learning, or 3D modelling.

The window is short, but that’s the point: see how far you can push what’s possible in a single evening. Mentors will be on the floor throughout, your work will be reviewed by a panel of industry judges, and every participant gets Cursor credits supported by Francisco Terpolilli, Cursor's EU Ambassador and Regional Leader.

Bring a team of 2-3, or turn up solo and we’ll help you find a crew, at our team formation session. Women, non-binary, and allies are all welcome.

[Prizes provided by PhysicsX](https://www.physicsx.ai/), including career coaching and mentorship opportunities, to be announced.

Bring your curiosity, your laptop, and your ambition. The city starts with you.

description:
AI 工具經常聽到，但到底怎樣用在「投資」上面？

學得再多功能，如果最後不能夠變成你的資產，其實完全沒有用。而 AI 最能夠落地的地方，一定是投資。

以前一間機構要一隊人才做得到的研究，今日一個人加一部電腦就做得到。

🎯 這一晚會講三件事

① 如何建立你的第一個 AI 員工

打造一個 ‘有記憶’ 的 AI ，24/7 隨時候命的私人員工。

description:
UPDATE: due to overwhelming demand, this event is now at capacity! Please register anyway to join the waiting list and we'll notify you if a seat is available. Thank you for your interest!

Hong Kong has moved beyond the question of whether crypto should be regulated. The harder question is how banks, securities firms, exchanges, and stablecoin payment providers make different regulatory regimes and control systems work together.

Basel III shapes how banks approach cryptoasset exposure. Securities and virtual asset firms face their own licensing, custody, and market-conduct obligations. Across the chain, compliance teams must detect financial crime using customer records, fiat transactions, wallet activity, and blockchain data that rarely sit in the same system.

One panel. Every side of the fiat–crypto boundary.

These speakers have sat on every side of the table: regulating financial markets, leading compliance inside banks and securities firms, operating global crypto exchanges, advising law enforcement, and applying those rules to stablecoin payments.

• Angelina Kwan, CEO at Stratford Finance Limited, formerly Global COO at BitMEX and HashKey Group, HKEX, and SFC.
• Avina Lobo, Regulatory Compliance Lead at Reap, formerly Animoca Brands and Bitget
• Debra Au, Co-chair of Global Coalition Fighting for Financial Crime APAC and Cyber Crime Policing Advisory Panel Member at Hong Kong Police Force. Previously Head of Financial Crime at HSBC HK, Societe Generale, and DBS.
• Lorraine Li, Head of Compliance at Mirae Asset Securities. Previously Head of Compliance Advisory at HSBC HK.
• Moderated by Teodora Irimia, Senior Account Executive, Flagright

Together, they will examine:

• Who monitors a transaction that passes through a bank, exchange, stablecoin provider, and self-hosted wallet?
• What changes when an established financial group acquires or partners with a crypto business?
• When is de-risking prudent, and when does it push activity beyond the regulated perimeter?
• What controls and evidence should regulators expect when monitoring spans both fiat and on-chain activity?

A practitioner-led discussion for people working in virtual assets, regulatory policy, compliance, payments, securities, and institutional treasury.

About the Event

We're excited to host a two-day, hands-on hackathon for curious, ambitious builders who want to go deep on physical AI. You'll get a real robot arm and support from Viam experts throughout.

No prior robotics experience is required, just an interest in physical AI and some software experience.

What You'll Build

Working in a team of 2-3, you'll build an end-to-end robotics application using Viam and a real robot arm.

Each team will have access to:

• UFactory xArm or Universal Robots arm with a two-finger gripper attachment (feel free to also bring your own SO-101)

• Charger plugging: Sub-centimeter precision, occlusion at the moment of contact
• Pouring liquid into a cup: Continuous control; a spill is a visible failure
• Recycling sort: Perception in clutter
• Egg transfer: Force control; failure is unambiguous and dramatic
• Jenga pull: Precision plus force feedback; the tower falling ends your run

2) Open: bring your own idea and get judged on ambition and execution.

• Ideas from past events: playing chess, mixing a cocktail, quality inspection, drawing a picture, puzzle insertion, setting a table, folding clothes.

name: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hackathon @ NYU
description:
## 📋 Event Description

Generative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, and candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, and TA practitioners who live this problem every week.

This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), and NYU — where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge.

🎯 The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel

Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel — recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, and candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, and that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it.

You can attack either side of the funnel — or the seam between them.

Side A — Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, and a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike — the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments — a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, and the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet. The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise — without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume.

Questions worth chasing:

• What signals — behavioral, identity, provenance — actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one?
• When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness?
• How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people?
• How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it?

Side B — Trust going out: impersonation and candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, and scam job seekers out of money and data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, and easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine.

Questions worth chasing:

• How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company?
• Can impersonating domains be detected and flagged early?
• What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter?

What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel and fits the way hiring actually happens — a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off and easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run.

You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here — that's the point of a single, focused theme. Engineers and builders can go straight at the detection, identity, and verification problems. HR-technology practitioners will be in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring actually works, and to pressure-test whether a recruiter would trust what you've made.

## Agent Harness Hackathon

Organized by TrueFoundry and HackerSquad. Sponsored by OpenAI.

AI agents are easy to prototype and much harder to run in production. Once an agent touches real users, tools, data, budgets, and internal systems, the work expands into routing, permissions, tracing, retries, evals, guardrails, cost controls, and deployment.

[Join TrueFoundry](https://www.truefoundry.com/) [and HackerSquad](https://hackersquad.io) for a full-day hackathon focused on building [production-minded agentic applications with TrueForge](https://trueforge.dev), [with sponsorship from OpenAI](https://openai.com/).

Take an agent use case from idea or prototype toward something you can observe, govern, evaluate, and operate. TrueFoundry’s AI Gateway, Agent Gateway, and MCP Gateway will frame the day, with practical work on model routing, controlled tool access, MCP workflows, observability, eval loops, fallback behavior, budget controls, and deployment.

Bring a laptop, a concrete use case, and a willingness to build under realistic production constraints.

## What You Can Build

• An agent workflow with model routing, retries, and fallback behavior
• A tool-using agent with controlled MCP or API access
• An observability layer for traces, tool calls, latency, usage, cost, and failures
• An eval or test harness for agent behavior across repeated runs
• A governance pattern for permissions, approvals, logging, blocking, or escalation
• An agent application that demonstrates how it could run inside a real team or platform environment

## The Challenges We’ll Explore

• Coordination: Connecting models, tools, permissions, memory, and context into reliable workflows
• Visibility: Understanding what an agent did, why it did it, and what changed between runs
• Reliability and cost: Managing quotas, budgets, latency, provider failures, retries, and fallbacks
• Runtime controls: Defining what data agents can access, which tools they can call, and when human approval is required
• Deployment: Connecting agents to internal systems while maintaining governance and reliability as usage grows

## Who Should Apply

• Platform, infrastructure, and backend engineers building or operating AI agent systems
• AI and product engineers working with LLMs, tool calling, MCP, evals, or agent workflows
• Technical founders moving agent prototypes toward production
• Security, DevOps, and ML platform practitioners working on governance, observability, and cost control
• Builders with a concrete agent use case and enough technical experience to build during the day

## Format

• Challenge brief, build tracks, and judging rubric
• Focused build time with technical support available
• Project submissions and supporting evidence

• Any teammates you plan to build with

description:
Calling all Moms….of kids, of projects, of pets; books; businesses. Mothers of the friend group, the boardroom, the classroom. We welcome you; we need you; we are you, and we wanna hear your voices. Come. Eat. Let’s chat.

If this offering caught your eye, it's for you. We invite you, and all people pondering the complexity of motherhood, to join us for dinner and dialogue. Whether you're a mother, hope to become one, or know definitively that you're not and are very pleased with that decision, this is a space for you.

Our aim is to bring unique thinkers  –  with hungry bellies  –  together to dialogue about the complex topic of motherhood. A special multi-course meal will fill your belly while fifteen other self identified moms fill the table. Through round-table discussion, guided breakout conversations, and moments for personal reflection, we invite you to open your heart and expand your mind around a topic you may have thought about often.

Your hosts, Sura Hertzberg and Gwen Pelfini, are licensed therapists who work with relationships and consciousness expansion. We've spoken at length about these questions  –  with each other, with our patients, with our friends and communities, and, naturally, with our own mothers. Too often our voices get siloed: we see the glossy Instagram stories, but we lack spaces for real dialogue. We're especially interested in spaces where people share not only from their own experience, but in how they relate to the experiences of others. Through reflective dialogue and other group tools, we hope to deepen and enrich how we all communicate and process together.

Food and the belly are their own complex questions for moms. We aim to feed your mind and your belly with equal intention — offering nourishment in every corner of your life, and caring deliberately for your digestive and your nervous system alike.

name: Battle of the Personal Brains Hackathon 🧠
description:
## 🧠 Cognee, AWS Strands Agent, Docker Sandbox, Bright Data

$100 in credits for everyone. $1000 in prizes for the winners!

Join us for Battle of the Personal Brains, a 5 hour hands-on AI hackathon where you’ll build an intelligent personal agent powered by your own data, live information, and create an agentic workflow to take action, all under one roof at the Bright Data office in SOMA.

Build the personal AI agent you’ve always wanted.

In today’s world, it’s possible for an AI agent to know what you know - your emails, your documents, meetings, calendar, tasks, files, and other information that’s relevant to you - and then act on it.

For this hackathon, the challenge is simple: Build a brain. Build an agent. Then make it do something.

## 🗓️ Event Details

• When: 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM, Monday September 21, 2026
• Where: Bright Data office, San Francisco, CA

## 🧠 First, Build your Personal Brain

Your agent is only as useful as the information it can understand. So you’ll create an AI-powered brain that can combine knowledge from multiple sources:

• Your laptop and local files
• Google Drive and cloud documents
• Personal email and other data sources
• Public information from across the web
• Meeting notes, receipts, photos, schedules, and more

You'll use Cognee’s structured AI memory to create your Personal Brain, and Bright Data to discover and retrieve public web data.

## 🤖 Then, Build your Agent

Once your agent can access the right knowledge, the real fun begins. Build an agent that can find information, reason across it, and take action.

Your agent could:

1. Manage your calendar - Find availability and schedule an appointment automatically.
2. Take notes and remind you later - Capture information and send a reminder exactly when you need it.
3. Turn meetings into action - Read meeting summaries, identify commitments and action items, and build your personal to-do schedule.
4. Handle your expenses - Process receipts, extract the important information, organize them, and prepare expense reports.
5. Organize and share your photos - Process photos, upload them to Google Photos, organize them, and share them with your WhatsApp group.
6. Build your own personal assistant - Create an agent that understands your information, remembers what's important, and helps you get things done.
7. Connect your digital life - Connect to apps and services you use every day, read through information, create notes, identify what matters, and remind you when action is required.

Or build something completely different.

Your brain. Your agent. Your idea.

## 🛠️ The Agentic Stack

We'll provide technologies you can combine to build your agent:

🧠 Cognee — The Brain - Create long-term AI memory and a Personal Brain that your agent can search, understand, and reason over. Get $50 of Cognee Cloud Credits.

🌐 Bright Data — The Web - Give your agent access to fresh public information from across the web. Get $50 of Bright Data Credits.

📁 Your Data — The Personal Brain - Bring your own files and information from your laptop, Google Drive, and other sources.

🤖 AWS Strands Agents — The Agent Harness - Build and orchestrate the agent that reasons, uses tools, and decides what to do next.

🐳 Docker Sandboxes — The Sandbox - Give your agent a secure environment where it can run code and perform tasks.

Together, these technologies give your agent something increasingly important:

Data + Memory + Reasoning + Tools + Actions

## ⚔️ The Battle

This isn't just about building another chatbot. We're looking for agents that can understand information and then accomplish something useful.

At the end of the hackathon, each team will demonstrate what their agents can do. Will it remember better? Find better information? Reason across personal, company, and public data? Can it take useful actions?

But most importantly: Can your brain beat the other brains?

## 👩‍💻 Who Should Attend?

Developers, AI engineers, agent builders, hackers, founders, students, and anyone interested in building the next generation of personal AI agents. You don't need to arrive with a finished idea. Come with a laptop, some curiosity, and a problem you'd love an AI agent to solve. We'll help you build the rest.

## 👩‍💻 What to Expect?

• $100 free credits ($50 from Cognee + $50 from Bright Data)
• $1000 in prizes for the top 3 winners! $500, $300, $200
• High-Energy Building Sessions: 5 hours to prototype cutting-edge data and agentic workflows
• Data & AI Challenges: Solve real-world problems that you and others can benefit from
• Expert Mentorship: On-site guidance from developer advocates from Cognee, AWS and Bright Data.
• Swag, Catering & Networking: Fuel up with snacks and food while connecting with fellow builders and founders.
• Prizes & Demos: Win prizes and pitch your build directly to industry leaders.

## 🚀 What You'll Leave With

By the end of the hackathon, you'll have gone beyond prompts and chatbots. You'll have built an agent with:

• A brain that remembers.
• Knowledge it can retrieve.
• Tools it can use.
• And the ability to take action.

Welcome to the Battle of the Personal Brains.

Despite a robust body of international humanitarian, human rights and criminal law addressing conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV), a persistent gap remains between international commitments and their effective implementation at the national level. This high-level panel will examine the case for a United Nations Framework Protocol on the Implementation of International Obligations relating to Conflict-Related Sexual Violence and Survivor-Centred Responses, a practical framework designed not to create new legal obligations, but to help States translate existing commitments into effective prevention, reporting and documentation, national response frameworks, justice and accountability, comprehensive referral mechanisms, and long-term support for victims and survivors. Building on existing international standards and good practices, including the Murad Code, the discussion will consider how a Framework Protocol could strengthen survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches, national coordination and international cooperation, while addressing emerging challenges and opportunities related to digital evidence, artificial intelligence and responsible innovation. The panel will bring together experts to identify priority implementation gaps and launch a global consultation process towards the development of the Framework Protocol.

As conflicts, repression and violence continue to affect communities worldwide, artificial intelligence presents new possibilities for ensuring that the voices and experiences of survivors are heard—while also raising critical questions about safety, dignity, consent, authenticity and the risk of retraumatization. This session will explore how AI and emerging technologies can be used responsibly to amplify survivor voices, preserve testimony, support truth-telling and accountability, and contribute to peacebuilding without exposing survivors to further harm, stigma or retaliation. Moderated through a trauma-informed lens, the discussion will examine what it means to place survivors, not technology, at the centre of innovation, including the safeguards needed to ensure meaningful consent, survivor agency and control over how testimony is collected, preserved and shared. Bringing together human rights advocates, practitioners and civil society leaders, the panel will consider how survivor-centred AI can help bridge the distance between lived experience and decision-making, ensuring that those most affected by violence and conflict are not simply subjects of international action, but active participants in shaping justice, reconciliation and sustainable peace.

name: Superpollutant Action Summit
description:
The Superpollutant Action Summit, convened by Beyond Alliance, is a first of its kind gathering for high-level leaders across business, science, government, and civil society to come together for a full day to accelerate action on the pollutants driving the most near-term warming: methane, black carbon, N₂O, and HFCs.

Rapid reductions over the next decade could meaningfully bend the warming curve before mid-century, making this one of the fastest and most immediate levers available for climate progress, with the added benefit of real air quality and health gains along the way.

Momentum on superpollutants has been building across governments, companies, and civil society, from the Global Methane Pledge to a wave of new corporate commitments like the Superpollutant Action Initiative, a $100 million effort from Amazon, Autodesk, Figma, Google, JPMorgan Chase, Salesforce, and Workday to fund high impact mitigation projects, coordinated by Beyond Alliance.

The event will bring together 150+ decision-makers driving climate action in business, finance, policy, and innovation. Through deep dives on corporate Scope 3 action, emerging market mechanisms, voluntary carbon markets, and the policies and financing needed to scale solutions, the day is built for candid dialogue and real commitments.

Across the day, expect candid actionable plenary conversations on where science, policy, and capital meet, thematic breakouts, a look at what it will take to finance faster action at scale, and a showcase of real solutions from the innovators and project developers building them.

description:
We've been programmed to think of banking as a utility: boring by design. Simply a safe place to park our money. A decision with little consequence beyond the financial.

Our everyday banking decisions generate massive emissions and fuel an invisible hand driving the climate crisis as well as social and environmental injustice around the world. In fact, research from Topo Finance found that, for many of the world's largest companies, the emissions generated by their cash and investments exceeded all their other emissions combined: their operations, their products, even their AI.

We have an opportunity to change that. By leveraging our financial management, we can drive positive impact and help transform the financial system into a visible hand for environmental and social progress around the world.

Join us for an exciting conversation about how corporations, municipalities, organisations and individuals are transforming their banking from one of their largest climate drivers into one of their greatest superpowers.

Readying the Little Red Dome -

The future of attritable aerial salvos will overwhelm traditional, sequential air defense systems. Revamp these legacy systems with the next generation of technology: With agentic AI, physics & digital twins at its core, compose robust defense products with commercially available technology. Build a new, comprehensive and investable idea that will secure safer skies. Getting sensors, C2, and shooters right is only half the battle. name: TOKEN2049 Singapore. Quantum Security for Digital Assets with Industry Leaders
description:
Quantum Security for Digital Assets

This private technical event brings together industry leaders, protocol engineers, cryptography researchers, digital asset specialists and institutional stakeholders to examine the emerging security requirements of digital assets in a post quantum environment.

The discussion will focus on the cryptographic foundations required to protect digital asset infrastructure as quantum computing develops, including digital signatures, transaction authentication, identity, key management, consensus security and the protection of blockchain execution environments.

Panels with industry leaders will be followed by relaxed networking with senior peers over food and drinks.

Particular attention will be given to the transition from conventional elliptic curve cryptography toward post quantum cryptographic systems and the practical considerations involved in implementing these mechanisms at protocol level.

Topics will include

• Post quantum digital signatures and transaction authentication
• Quantum resistant identity and account structures
• Key generation, address derivation and key lifecycle management
• Post quantum consensus and validator communication
• Cryptographic verification within distributed systems
• Quantum resistant smart contract infrastructure
• Migration considerations for existing digital asset systems
• Security implications for institutional digital asset custody and infrastructure.
• The discussion will also examine how post quantum cryptography can be integrated throughout a blockchain protocol rather than being implemented as an isolated security layer.

Quantova will present its approach to post quantum blockchain architecture, including the Quantova Virtual Machine and its implementation of PQR cryptographic primitives across transaction signing, account creation, consensus and execution.

Attendees will have the opportunity to examine the practical relationship between cryptographic primitives, protocol architecture and application execution, with discussion focused on implementation rather than commercial promotion.

About organizers:

• [Quantova](https://Quantova.org) runs a post-quantum Layer 1 network built from first principles to issue, move, settle and protect digital value: digital identity, stablecoins, tokenised real-world assets, payments and institutional settlement, without inheriting a future migration burden.
• [Quantova launched QDock.io](https://QDock.io), the development environment supporting post quantum application development, together with the underlying cryptographic libraries, compilation tooling and deployment infrastructure used within the Quantova environment.

[Further technical information is available at Quantova.org](https://Quantova.org)

HackenProof is a bug bounty and crowdsourced security platform connecting companies with a global network of white-hat security researchers. The platform supports more than 400 programs, with over $26 million paid in bounties and a community of more than 85,000 ethical hackers.

Anna Tutova has been active in the digital asset industry for many years, working at the intersection of cryptocurrency regulation, institutional finance and quantum security. She has contributed to international regulatory and industry discussions and spoken at events across multiple regions, including on the evolving relationship between digital assets, regulation and post-quantum security.
